### GWSTransport

``` python
def GWSTransport(
    *args, gcls:NoneType=None, creds:NoneType=None, **kwargs
):
```

*Thin async transport over httpx. By default each request gets a fresh
client, so nothing is tied to an event loop; pass `client=` to use a
persistent client that you manage (and close via `aclose`).*

``` python
creds = await oauth_creds(scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly',
                                  'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly'],
                          redirect_uri='https://oauth.appapis.org/redirect')
```

``` python
drive = GWSApi('drive', creds=creds)
fs = await drive.files.list(q="name contains 'fastgws' and trashed=false", page_size=10)
fs, fs.files[0]
```

``` python
gmail = GWSApi('gmail', creds=creds)
msgs = await gmail.users.messages.list(user_id='me', max_results=10)
len(msgs['messages'])
```

    10

If a request comes back 401 (an expired or revoked access token), the
transport refreshes the credentials, retries, and saves the fresh token
back to the token file – so long-running processes never need to re-run
`oauth_creds`.

``` python
creds.token = 'not-a-valid-token'
msgs = await gmail.users.messages.list(user_id='me', max_results=1)
test_eq(json.loads(Path(creds.token_path).read_text())['token'], creds.token)
```

``` python
reqs = [(m.id, gmail._gservice.users().messages().get(userId='me', id=m.id)) for m in msgs.messages]
res = gmail.batch_get(reqs)
len(res)
```

    10

``` python
url = 'https://fast-http-bin.pla.sh/status/'
status = 500

t = time.time()
try: await gmail.transport.request('GET', url + str(status), base=0.05)
except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
    assert time.time() - t > 1
    test_eq(e.response.status_code, status)
    test_eq(e.api_error().retryable, True)
```

``` python
status = 400

t = time.time()
try: await gmail.transport.request('GET', url + str(status), base=0.05)
except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
    assert time.time() - t < .5
    test_eq(e.response.status_code, status)
    test_eq(e.api_error().retryable, False)
```
